chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ibn Ribat from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I heard your father saying that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave a choice to his wives, so they chose Allah and His Messenger, so he did not keep them upon a divorce, and if they had chosen themselves, they would have been irrevocably divorced.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'This is a hadith which my father used to narrate from Aisha. And what is for the people and the choice? Rather, this is something which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, specialized His Messenger with.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet's choice of his wives and the general ruling for people?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the theological distinction between the specific privilege of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) and the general ruling for his wives during the event of Khuruj (The Choice). Imam al-Rida (AS) explains that while the narration attributed to his father referenced Aisha, the unique condition that they would not be divorced if they chose the Prophet was a special divine concession (Khasiyya) for the Prophet alone, not a universal legal precedent for all Muslims.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad, and Ibn Rabat, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I heard your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> saying that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> (gave) a choice to his<sup>saww</sup> wives, so they chose Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> did not keep them upon a divorce, and had they chosen themselves, they would have been irrevocably divorced’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a Hadeeth which my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> had reported about Ayesha. And what is for the people and the choice? But rather, this is something which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Specialised His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> with’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and ibn Ribat from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that I once heard your father saying, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, offered his wives the choice and they chose Allah and His Messenger. He did not keep them for divorce. Had they chosen themselves they would become strangers.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is a Hadith that my father would narrate from ‘A’ishah. What people have to do with choice! It was something with which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, specially treated His Messenger.’”
